Nina: FYI we got a bug report: Next/Edge app fails with `require is not defined` and some TS consumers see `process is not defined`. Repro on Vercel Edge.

Evan: likely resolution problem. Can you paste package.json exports from the installed package?

Nina: installed package.json shows: main -> dist/cjs/index.js, module -> dist/esm/index.js, types -> dist/types/index.d.ts, exports only has ./package.json mapping.

Rosa: yeah that will cause some ESM runtimes/bundlers to pick the CJS entry or miss types. Two-pronged fix: add conditional exports mapping and make top-level types point at a canonical d.ts entry.

Evan: propose this minimal mapping:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "types": "./dist/esm/index.d.ts",
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
    "default": "./dist/esm/index.js"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```

Rosa: Also ensure both builds are produced from the same compiled artifacts so auth/retry logic doesn't diverge between esm and cjs. Add a smoke test that imports both outputs and runs the same auth/retry scenario.

Nina: I'll prepare a canary with the export mapping and a small CI job that runs the `examples/next-edge` in headless vercel dev (or at least executes an ESM import in a simulated edge environment).

ci-bot: queued canary build @redwood/sdk@canary-0.2.7 (esm/cjs + types).

Evan: once canary is up, run TS compile against TS 4.5, 4.8 and 5.0 to catch resolver differences. If we still see `process` at runtime, drop `main` or set it to ESM with CJS wrapper.

Rosa: add a tiny README checklist: export mapping, top-level types, sourcemap normalization, and parity smoke tests. Saves future iterations.

Nina: PR opened with changes + CI: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/358 — will attach canary results when build finishes.
